instructions: In a small saucepan, off the heat, stir together the soy sauce, mirin, sugar, 5 tbsp of water, the ginger and the garlic, grated. In a cup, mix the cornstarch with 1 tbsp of water.
Put the saucepan over medium heat and bring it to a boil. Stir in the cornstarch mixture and cook for 30 seconds until the sauce is glossy and thick. Take it off the heat.

Slice the onion half thinly. Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the onion for 6 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's soft and browned at the edges. Transfer it to a bowl.
Meanwhile, put the beef in a bowl with the salt and pepper and mix it lightly. Overworking it makes tough burgers. Divide it into 4 portions and press each into a patty about 1/2 inch thick.
Wipe out the skillet, add 1 tbsp of the oil, and heat it over medium-high. Add the patties and cook for 4 minutes without moving them, until the underside is deep brown. Flip them.
While the patties cook, heat the last 1 tbsp of oil in a second pan over medium-high heat. Cook the pineapple rings for 2 minutes on each side until browned.

Cook the burgers for 3 minutes. Brush each with 1 tbsp of the sauce and top with a slice of cheddar. Cover the pan for 1 minute to melt the cheese. You're cooking the burgers to 160°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check one there. No thermometer? Cut into one: it's done when there's no pink left.
Toast the buns, cut side down, in the empty skillet for 1 minute. Shred 2 lettuce leaves and slice the tomato.
Spread 1 tbsp of the mayonnaise on each bottom bun. Add the lettuce, tomato, a patty, a pineapple ring and the onion. Spoon 1 tbsp of the remaining sauce on top and add the top bun.
method_notes: Lead is Just One Cookbook's teriyaki burger (4.8 from 5): a seasoned beef patty brushed with teriyaki sauce and cheddar at the end, with grilled pineapple, onion, lettuce, tomato and Japanese mayonnaise. No version has 20 ratings, so the fallback flag is set. Its caramelized onion takes 25 minutes, so the onion is browned for 6 minutes instead, and the patties are pan-cooked. That page links its sauce rather than printing it; the sauce here uses the soy, mirin, sugar, ginger, garlic and cornstarch proportions of RecipeTin Japan's teriyaki burger, with water in place of the sake. Recipe Girl's burger (5.0 from 1) mixes pineapple into the patty.
